title: Working out when he started and the 1902 move to New Orleans
summary: Dating his start at six or seven, the family's connection to the McCalls, his brother going to New Orleans, and his mother taking him there in 1902.

blocks.x: Now you see. See, I was playing along before I figured out in 97. How many years would that be?
Nineteen seven is fifty years ago. Exactly. Nineteen fifty-seven. That made me buck. Nineteen seven you'd be fifteen years old. Yeah, I was playing a long before that.
Well, that's when I grew up in the big band. See, because I was playing good eight years before that.

As far as I can remember back, because I know I was around seven, six or seven. You see, that's the closest I'll get back to when I started, because I don't know when I started. See, I figured my husband had been around six or seven. Which would be about 1900, 1902, something like that.
Yeah, about 1900. Wait a minute. In 1900 you were eight years old.
Wait a minute, wait a minute. 1902, my mother carried me to New Orleans.
You were ten years old then?
Yeah, around ten or eleven, between ten and eleven. The seat of Mardi Gras.
Is that the first time you went to the city?
Yeah, because I made 11 years old that year I think. See. And well I was playing before that.

See, because my brother, see the McCall, the people that we raised, he got married I think in 1900. I remember driving him to the station. My brother? No. The McCalls, the people that we raised, the sons. See I had to go with them to drive the buggy back, because they got to trade and they go to New Orleans. And I went after they got settled, about 1901. They were in Mardi Gras. See my brother was in New Orleans, he was in New Orleans about a year from when my mother met there. They got married in 1901, in the summer time, and we went to New Orleans, the next year, February. But we was playing before then, around there, because they broke up our little band. So when you went to? When my brother went to New Orleans, to work for those people. He was waiting tables like my daddy was doing, see. Then my mother moved there. Then my mother went to New Orleans, and we was in New Orleans about a place or not to be speaking.
